en.title: Software After Scarcity: The Commoditization of Code and Technological Labor
en.deck: The internet, open source, globally traded labor and AI have lowered the costs of technological production. Their cumulative effect may redistribute income between workers, software vendors and owners of complementary capital.
en.regime: Declining implementation costs and uneven labor demand.
en.key_risk: Entry-level opportunities and income distribution may deteriorate even as output rises.

pt-BR.title: O software depois da escassez: a comoditização do código e do trabalho tecnológico
pt-BR.deck: Internet, código aberto, globalização do trabalho e IA reduziram os custos da produção tecnológica. Seus efeitos cumulativos podem redistribuir renda entre trabalhadores, fornecedores de software e proprietários de capital complementar.
pt-BR.regime: Redução dos custos de implementação e demanda desigual por trabalho.
pt-BR.key_risk: Oportunidades de entrada e distribuição da renda podem deteriorar-se mesmo com expansão da produção.

signal_rationale.delta: Commoditization of implementation and labor scarcity, distinct from a daily technology signal.
signal_rationale.evidence: ITU connectivity, BLS projections, Stanford HAI and Digital Economy Lab, NBER and ILO.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Knowledge diffusion and reusable infrastructure lower implementation cost; AI accelerates selected execution tasks.
signal_rationale.transmission: Lower cost and expanded supply change substitution, wage bargaining and complementary asset rents.
signal_rationale.falsifier: Persistent growth in real wages and entry-level hiring for standardized tasks relative to validated output would weaken the thesis.

key_constraints: No harmonized global surplus measure; US data cannot establish worldwide displacement.
AI exposure and employment association are not causal estimates.

producer_checks.novelty_decision: Historical labor supply and product economics, differentiated from infrastructure-focused digital abundance research.
